images.filename: Papakolea Beach - South Point, Kona (Big Island), Hawaii.jpg
images.caption: Panoramic view of the Papakōlea Beach as seen from the green sands on the beach. One of four green sand beaches in the world, the sand is acquires it's distinctive olivine green coloring due to erosion from the enclosing volcanic cone (tuff ring). The fragmental volcanic material (pyroclastics) of the tuff ring contain olivine, a silicate mineral containing iron and magnesium, also known as peridot when of gem quality.
images.alt: Panoramic view of the Papakōlea Beach as seen from the green sands on the beach. One of four green sand beaches in the world, the sand is acquires it's distinctive olivine green coloring due to erosion from the enclosing volcanic cone (tuff ring). The fragmental volcanic material (pyroclastics) of the tuff ring contain olivine, a silicate mineral containing iron and magnesium, also known as peridot when of gem quality.

images.caption:
This is one of very few green sand beaches in the world. Ride to this beach is quite an adventure. There is no easy way to go here unless you have UTV or high-powered all wheel drive. We hitched a ride with a local gentleman named John for $15 round trip pp. There is no proper road to reach here, its all just roughest terrain with mud puddles, rocks and whatnot. We saw so many 'all terrain' SUVs stuck on the way here. 


Dont even think about driving your rental car here.

images.caption: South point on the Big Island of Hawaii is the southern most point of United States. Going south from south point will take one directly to Antarctica. South point is about one and half hour drive from Kailua Kona and about one hour and forty five minutes from the town of Hilo. From the south point, one can hike for 3 miles to get to the secluded Green Sand Beach which is one of the only 2 beaches in the world with naturally occurring green sand. Green sand is formed by the gemstone Olivine. Instead of hiking, you can also drive if you have a high 4x4 drive vehicle. Some locals my also give you ride back and forth for about $15 each person. It is definitely worth the trip and life time opportunity to view green sand.
